name: Le Code de l'honneur
editorial_article: Le Code de l'honneur is the debut studio album by French rapper Rohff, released on December 7, 1999. A seminal work in the landscape of French hip-hop, the album solidified Rohff's reputation as a key figure in the scene, blending hardcore rap sensibilities with the boom bap production typical of the era. The project was released through Phénomène Records, the label of T.I.N from Expression Direkt, alongside Musisoft Distribution and EMI. Spanning over 74 minutes, the album is noted for its gritty lyricism and its deep integration into the Mafia K'1 Fry collective, featuring collaborations with prominent members such as 113, OGB, Intouchable, and Karlito. Tracks like 'Du fond du cœur' and 'Génération sacrifiée' have since become recognized as classics of the genre. The album remains a cornerstone of late 90s French rap, capturing the raw energy and social commentary that defined the period.
editorial_pitch: The debut studio album from French rap icon Rohff, Le Code de l'honneur is a foundational classic of the late 90s French hip-hop scene.
